brief: Broadcom closed its $63 billion "North Star" SPV to finance Anthropic's chip purchases only after agreeing to pay higher interest and guarantee residual value equal to the roughly $43.5 billion (69%) first lien, after some lenders got cold feet; so Broadcom, the seller of the chips, now backstops the loan that buys them. That guarantee stacks on Big Sky's $29 billion backstop and a $42 billion convertible note, for roughly $114 billion of Broadcom exposure to Anthropic before OpenAI financing is even sized. Anthropic's S-1 shows $637 billion of compute commitments against $16.3 billion of first-half revenue and an $80 billion six-month paper loss, so first-lien lenders are effectively buying Broadcom credit, not Anthropic risk; Blackstone's second lien carries the real AI-lab risk. Credit markets already price this: Broadcom's CDS sits near record wides, the IG hyperscaler basket had its worst week outside July, and USD CCC spreads sit at the 100th percentile of three years. Meta's $97.5 billion raise and the deal's completion gave credit a one-day bid, but it had already faded by Tuesday morning.
